description.html: Mealworms are small larvae with a tougher outer skin and a higher fat content. Lizards eat them eagerly because they keep moving, so they are a favorite addition to the diet of bearded dragons, leopard geckos and other insect eaters. Because of their composition, they are not a staple food but a treat and a supplement to dubia roaches and other feeder insects.

Feed mealworms in moderation, a few times a week alongside the main food, not every day. They are good for building condition in thinner animals, after winter rest or as a reward. They are easiest to offer in a smooth bowl they cannot climb out of, so they do not burrow into the substrate. Dust them with calcium before feeding.

Mealworms can be kept in the fridge in a box with bran or rolled oats: the cold slows their development into pupae and beetles, so they last longer. Before feeding, leave them at room temperature for a short while so they become active. Read more about feeding on our lizard food page.
